en: Washing hands after gardening prevents hookworm larvae in soil from entering your body through cuts.
Emptying stagnant water around your house stops Aedes mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever.
Drinking eight glasses of water daily helps your kidneys filter urea waste from your blood.
Never eat wild mushrooms because some species contain amatoxins that cause severe, fatal liver failure.
Washing a dog bite with soap and water for fifteen minutes significantly reduces rabies infection risk.
Avoid swimming in floodwaters because rat urine in the water transmits the leptospirosis bacteria to humans.
Eating carrots provides vitamin A, which your eye retina requires to maintain healthy vision in dim light.
Avoid touching stray cat feces because it can contain Toxoplasma gondii parasites that cause human infection.
Wearing a mask during dry, windy days prevents inhaling airborne plant pollen that triggers allergic asthma.
Tucking your pants into your socks while hiking prevents forest ticks from crawling onto your bare skin.
Getting fifteen minutes of morning sunlight helps your skin produce vitamin D to absorb bone-strengthening calcium.
Sweat and dark clothing attract bees, so shower and wear light colors outdoors to avoid stings.
